text:
maya: Seeing a weird oscillation in streaming sessions on prod -> tenants get bounced between edges every ~60s, spikes reconnects and duplicate billing entries. Console shows sticky route flips but the telemetry tag is vague.

maya: Example trace: `resume_id=none -> auth-sticky=expired -> reconnect -> resume_id=new` repeated.

maya: Noticed this started ~09:40UTC, coincides with the session-affinity v1.3 canary.

tj: ugh. do we have logs per-tenant? can you paste the minimal logs?

maya: pasted snippet below from proxy logs: ```
[09:41:02] tenant=acct-42 conn=abcd auth_token=tok-xyz sticky_expires=2026-03-21T09:41:01Z resume_id=
[09:41:03] tenant=acct-42 conn=abcd reconnect reason=sticky-expiry new_resume=res-123
[09:41:04] tenant=acct-42 conn=efgh routed->edge-7 sticky_set=res-123
[09:41:05] tenant=acct-42 conn=abcd reconnect reason=route-swap resume=res-123
```

sylvia: console is sampling streaming telemetry aggressively; we don't surface the resume_id or sticky cookie lifetime right now. that makes it hard to attribute.

jordan: is the canary toggling a different sticky TTL or a change to how we compute affinity?

maya: according to the rollout notes, v1.3 added a fallback where expired auth keys still get a short-lived sticky (60s) instead of immediate invalidation. seems plausible it's the culprit.

tj: if expired keys leave a sticky that short, clients will churn on token rotation. looks like a path to oscillation. we need to know whether it's the auth layer or the proxy TTL.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: session-affinity v1.3 -> 10% traffic started at 2026-03-21T09:30Z. :rocket:

ops-bot: Alert triggered: streaming-reconnect-rate for region-us-west > 3x baseline at 09:41.

sylvia: proposal: add `resume_id` and `sticky_ttl` to the console streaming samples (low-cardinality tags) and a per-tenant reconnect count metric. That will make the pattern obvious in dashboards.

jordan: short-term mitigation: revert v1.3 canary or disable the short-lived fallback. long-term: push resume_id through tracing so we can correlate reconnects to billing events.

maya: agree. also request adding `X-Resume-ID` header in the proxy-to-runtime handoff so downstream traces include it.

tj: I can sketch the header patch. quick question: will adding `X-Resume-ID` affect our cache keys? we should avoid coupling it to kvcache unless intentional.

sylvia: don't change kvcache for now. header only for telemetry/traces. we can land a UI change to surface it in the console logs panel.

jordan: ops, are we ok rolling back the canary? status?

ops-bot: Rollback scheduled: session-affinity v1.3 canary -> rolling back 10% traffic at 09:45Z per ops playbook.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated.

maya: after rollback I still want a short postmortem entry: root cause hypothesis, timeline, and the proposed telemetry changes. I'll start a doc.

tj: next dev tasks: (1) add X-Resume-ID header, (2) add resume_id and sticky_ttl tags to streaming sample exporter, (3) increment tenant reconnect counter in metrics pipeline. I'll open PRs.

sylvia: console work: add a dashboard panel showing reconnects by tenant + resume_id distribution. also add an annotation when affinity-related rollouts change.

jordan: double-check billing dedupe logic: we might be double-charging during oscillation windows. ops, can you enable a short query to look for duplicate token usage across consecutive reconnects?

ops-bot: Query scheduled. will post results in this thread.

maya: thanks all. provisional priority: P1 for dashboard+metrics (visibility), P2 for header+patch, P3 for billing audit. :eyes:
